title: Signal Index & Prioritization - Runtime Regression Runlog
body:
Summary:
This is a working runlog for how we synthesize noisy observability signals into a prioritized regression triage path. The goal is to (1) avoid immediate panic for marginal blips, (2) collect deterministic artifacts for bisecting, and (3) enable fast canary comparisons and rollbacks. Use this doc as the team’s canonical checklist + example log for future incidents.

Why this exists (motivation):
- We repeatedly see multi-metric regressions where the root cause sits in an orthogonal layer (kernel scheduler, NCCL, model kernel selection). Alerts fire across latency percentiles, CPU steal, GPU mem fragmentation, and throughput throttles.
- Current triage often scatters — one engineer runs flamegraphs, another compares canary vs main, and we lose timestamps/queries. We need a compact index of signals to prioritize and the minimal artifact set to repro / bisect.

Prioritization heuristic (short):
1) Customer impact first: elevated 99th/95th latency on a production path observed for > 5m and affecting > 10% of requests.
2) Correlated error increase: retry loops, 5xxs, or model errors within the same time window.
3) Resource drift: GPU utilization delta > 15pp vs historical baseline for same traffic mix OR CPU steal > 5%.
4) Infrastructure signals: pod restarts, OOMs, kernel messages (dmesg) in same timeframe.
5) Canary delta: if a canary with identical config shows no regression, prioritize routing/config differences; if canary matches, suspect platform-level regression.

Minimum artifact collection (what to gather immediately):
- Grafana dashboard snapshot (panels: token-per-second, 50/95/99 latency, queue depth, GPU util/power, CPU steal) + UTC timestamp range.
- Prometheus queries used (save exact PromQL). Example: 
  - latency_99p_over_time = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
  - request_q_depth = sum(queue_length) by (node)
- A 30s pprof profile / perf on serving process (if safe) with build id noted.
- Serving runtime logs for the interval (+ 5m before, + 10m after). Include request IDs for sample slow traces.
- KV cache hit rates and eviction counts.
- Canary snapshot metadata: model version, quantization profile, kernel flags, runtime binary git sha.
- Synthetic load script used for replay (if any) and traffic replay plan.

Triage flow (ordered checklist):
- Phase 0: Rate-limit the noise
  - Silence non-actionable alerts on the channel and open an incident in JIRA with a single incident lead.
- Phase 1: Confirmation & scope
  - Confirm 99/95 deviance vs baseline for the same traffic distribution. Record PromQL timestamps and thresholds.
  - Identify affected routes and percentages. Use route tag in traces.
- Phase 2: Quick differentiators (5–15 min)
  - Compare primary vs canary: run PromQL diff snapshot over same timeframe. If canary ok -> config/placement vs if canary also bad -> infra/runtime.
  - Check model binary version changes and rollout logs.
  - Inspect recent infra deploys (kube nodes, driver updates, scheduling changes).
- Phase 3: Artifact capture for bisect (15–60 min)
  - Collect a deterministic slow request sample (request id + input) for replay.
  - Snapshot the runtime binary SHA, and any dynamic kernel selection logs.
  - Run microbenchmarks locally or in lab: single-request latency, KV lookup time, attention-kernel time. Keep parameters identical to production sample (seq len, batch size, prompt shape).
- Phase 4: Targeted profiling and hypothesis test (1–4 hr)
  - CPU/GPU flamegraphs and nvprof traces on repro run.
  - Toggle one factor at a time on a canary: disable batching, change kernel flag, pin model version, change quantization profile. Record delta.
  - If change reverts regression, create a hotfix PR with a minimal revert/tweak and run canary.

Example incident log (abridged):
- 2026-01-12T15:03Z: Pager alert: serving-high-latency-99 fired for route /chat/completions (alerts channel #perf). 99th rose from 120ms to 410ms over 7m.
- 15:05Z: Owner (Lina) triaged. Snapshot saved: grafana://dash/serving-runtime?from=2026-01-12T14:50Z&to=2026-01-12T15:20Z.
- 15:09Z: Confirmed canary (canary-03) did NOT show the spike. Diff indicated node-level placement skew: affected nodes were a new node pool with 24.1 kernel driver.
- 15:20Z: Collected pprof (30s) and nvprof traces from a repro run on one affected node. Noted kernel selection log showing fallback to slow int8 kernel.
- 16:15Z: Hotfix: force-switch kernel selector to fast path on canary; 30m canary passed. Rollout to main scheduled after further canary stability window.
- Postmortem: cause: new node kernel driver introduced non-deterministic scheduling causing heavy syscall latency that triggered the runtime to choose a different kernel fallback.

Dashboard/Queries (practical snippets to save in incident):
- Baseline comparison query (PromQL): 
  sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="serving",route=~"/chat.*"}[5m])) by (le)
- GPU mem fragmentation: 
  avg_over_time(gpu_memory_free_bytes[10m]) / avg_over_time(gpu_memory_total_bytes[10m])
- KV cache hit rate: 
  sum(kv_cache_hits_total{job="serving"}) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total{job="serving"})

Common false positives and how to dismiss quickly:
- Single-bastard host blip: check node restarts, host-level dmesg. If isolated to one node and canary on other nodes is ok, deprioritize cluster-wide rollback.
- Synthetic traffic artifact: correlate with client-side retry storms (client_id) and upstream proxies.
- Minor 95th jitter during rollout: if not affecting 99th and error rates unchanged, set to monitor and re-evaluate after window.

Bisect primers (how to set up a quick AB for kernels):
- Create two canaries with identical traffic split (5% each) but different kernel selector FLAGS. Ensure identical placement constraints and node types.
- Use traffic shadowing instead of full routing for latency-insensitive endpoints.
- Automate comparison dashboard that shows per-canary latency percentiles + resource deltas.

Open questions / TODOs (items to follow up):
- Can we add an automatic artifact packer that grabs grafana snapshots + PromQL + logs into the JIRA when an alert fires? (owner: Platform eng, ticket: JIRA-ENG-1489)
- Improve canary placement: exclude new node pools for first 48h after kernel/driver upgrades. (owner: infra)
- Add a simple binary metric: "kernel-fallback-rate" exposed by runtime to make kernel fallbacks signalable. (owner: serving-runtime)
- Document standard repro parameters for model microbenchmarks (seq len, batch mix, prompt tokens) and land as a small script. (owner: applied-ml)

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep this doc concise. When under pressure, step back to the heuristic and artifact list. Too many fancy profiling steps slow down the resolution.
- If you get a single sample that reproduces reliably, you win. Focus early on deterministic repro rather than chasing transient PromQL noise.
- Add a tiny section with common PromQL snippets on the team handbook page.

Appendix (quick commands):
- Capture pprof: go tool pprof -seconds 30 http://serving-node:6060/debug/pprof/profile
- Collect recent logs: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=\"prod-serving\" AND timestamp>\"2026-01-12T14:50:00Z\"" --limit 5000 > incident-logs.txt
- Run microbench (local repro): ./tools/microbench --model xgen-3b --seq 512 --batch 1 --seed-request-id <id>

If you add items or run an incident off this template, append a short summary (2–3 lines) at the top and tag with the incident JIRA. Keep the body as the canonical artifact manifest for any triage.

Unresolved emendations: we should align on where the canonical canary config lives (console vs infra repo) — put this on next retro agenda.

End of runlog.
